exercises.statement: The income statement of a UK private company opens with the line "Turnover: £8.4m". What does this figure represent?
options: The proportion of employees who left the company during the year
The total assets of the company at year-end
Revenue from the sale of goods and services (chiffre d'affaires)
The number of times inventories were sold and replaced during the year
exercises.explanation: Option 3 is correct: in British accounts, "turnover" is the traditional word for revenue from the sale of goods and services, i.e. the French "chiffre d'affaires"; IFRS uses "revenue". Option 1 is wrong: that is "staff turnover" (rotation du personnel), an HR indicator, not an accounting figure. Option 2 is wrong: total assets is a balance sheet total, not a performance figure. Option 4 is wrong: "inventory turnover" (rotation des stocks) is a ratio; on its own, "turnover" in the accounts means revenue.
exercises.source_ref: UK statutory formats: the Large and Medium-sized Companies and Groups (Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/410, Schedule 1) and the Small Companies and Groups (Accounts and Directors' Report) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/409), made under the Companies Act 2006, use "turnover" ; IFRS 15 (règlement UE 2023/1803) and IFRS 18 §75(a)(i) (formerly IAS 1 §82(a); règlement UE 2023/1803 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/338) use "revenue"

exercises.statement: In IAS 36 Impairment of Assets, the "recoverable amount" (valeur recouvrable) of an asset is defined as:
options: The lower of its fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use
Its cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses
Its fair value less costs of disposal, whatever its value in use
The higher of its fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use
exercises.explanation: Option 4 is correct: IAS 36 §18 defines recoverable amount as the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use; an impairment loss is recognised when the carrying amount exceeds this amount (§59). Option 1 is wrong: it takes the lower of the two values, a common confusion with the inventory rule (lower of cost and net realisable value, IAS 2). Option 2 is wrong: that describes the carrying amount (valeur nette comptable), which is compared with recoverable amount. Option 3 is wrong: fair value less costs of disposal is only one of the two measures used.

exercises.statement: In US English, "stock" usually refers to a company's shares (e.g. "common stock"), whereas in the accounts of a UK company the word "stock" has traditionally meant inventories.
exercises.justification: True: US "common stock" = ordinary shares, while UK "stock" = inventories (IFRS: "inventories").
exercises.explanation: In traditional UK accounts, "stock" (or "stocks") means goods held for sale or for use in production (stocks in French); the US equivalent is "inventory", and IFRS uses "inventories" (IAS 2). In US English, "stock" refers to equity shares: "common stock" (actions ordinaires), "preferred stock" (actions de préférence), "stockholders' equity" (capitaux propres). When reading an English-language document, the origin (UK or US) of the text determines the meaning of "stock".
exercises.source_ref: Usual UK and US accounting terminology ; IAS 2 uses "inventories" (règlement UE 2023/1803)

exercises.front: In IFRS terminology, what is the difference between "depreciation" and "amortisation", and how do they translate into French?
exercises.back:
Depreciation: systematic allocation of the cost of property, plant and equipment over its useful life (IAS 16).
Amortisation: the same mechanism for intangible assets (IAS 38).
Both translate as "amortissement".
Trap: "dépréciation" in French means an impairment loss (IAS 36), not depreciation.
exercises.explanation: Both terms describe the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life. IFRS reserves "depreciation" for tangible assets and "amortisation" (US spelling: amortization) for intangible assets. The French "dépréciation" is a false friend: it corresponds to an impairment loss, recognised when the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount (IAS 36).
exercises.source_ref: IAS 16 §6 (depreciation) ; IAS 38 §8 (amortisation) ; IAS 36 §6 (impairment loss) — règlement UE 2023/1803

exercises.statement:
Note 12 of the IFRS accounts of Calder Packaging plc describes a production line at 31 December 2025 (€k): cost 1,500; accumulated depreciation 600; no previous impairment. Because of a fall in demand, the line is tested for impairment. Its fair value is 730 and the costs of disposal would be 30; its value in use (present value of the future cash flows) is 760.

Calculate the impairment loss to be recognised, in €k (enter 0 if there is none).
exercises.explanation: Carrying amount = cost − accumulated depreciation = 1,500 − 600 = 900. Fair value less costs of disposal = 730 − 30 = 700. Recoverable amount = the higher of 700 and 760 = 760 (IAS 36 §18). Impairment loss = 900 − 760 = 140, recognised in profit or loss (IAS 36 §59-60); in French, a dépréciation of 140 k€. Taking the lower value (900 − 700 = 200) or ignoring costs of disposal and value in use (900 − 730 = 170) are the classic errors.
exercises.source_ref: IAS 36 §6, §18 and §59-60 ; IAS 16 §6 (carrying amount) — règlement UE 2023/1803

exercises.statement: Which of the following items is recognised in other comprehensive income (OCI, autres éléments du résultat global) rather than in profit or loss?
options: A gain on the disposal of a delivery van
An exchange difference on a trade payable denominated in US dollars
A revaluation surplus on land measured under the revaluation model
exercises.explanation: Option 4 is correct: an increase in carrying amount arising on revaluation is recognised in OCI and accumulated in equity under the heading revaluation surplus (IAS 16 §39), unless it reverses a revaluation decrease previously recognised in profit or loss. Option 1 is wrong: an impairment loss on goodwill is recognised in profit or loss (IAS 36 §60) and is never reversed. Option 2 is wrong: a gain on derecognition of an item of PP&E is included in profit or loss (IAS 16 §68). Option 3 is wrong: exchange differences on settling or translating monetary items such as trade payables are recognised in profit or loss (IAS 21 §28).
exercises.source_ref: IFRS 18 appendix A and B87 (other comprehensive income; formerly IAS 1 §7) — règlement UE 2023/1803 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/338 ; IAS 16 §39 and §68 ; IAS 21 §28 ; IAS 36 §60 — règlement UE 2023/1803
